Messages.Author: VTES2004
Messages.Body:
This is boring illustration of VTES game procedure which I am
fascinated with for no apparent reason other than they seem woefully
inadequately defined in the rulebook.

Setup-

The Order of Players' seating
MethA
MethB
MethC
MethD
MethE (MethE's prey is MethA)

consider:

0. MethA's minion phase
1. MethA declares bleed against MethB with VampA
2. MethB has option to respond (let's say attempt block)
3. MethC has option to respond (Eagle's Sight,Bauble, whatever...)
4. MethD has option to respond
5. MethE has option to respond
6. MethA has option to respond

Seems simple enough if it is correct but it's not according to my
digging in the newsgroup.

This flow demonstrates the flow within reason:

1. MethA declares bleed against MethB with VampA
(Has option to play as many effects as she wants)
MethE activates a sup. bauble
MethE activates a sup. bauble
Pass

2. MethB has option to respond
(Has option to play as many effects as she wants)
MethB attempts to block with VampB
MethE activates a sup. bauble
MethE activates a sup. bauble
Pass

3. MethC has option to respond
MethC activates a sup. bauble.
MethC play's sup eagle sight on VampC
Pass

4. MethD has option to respond
Pass

5. MethE has option to respond
(MethE has option to play as many effects as she wants)
MethE activates a sup. bauble
MethE activates a sup. bauble
MethE burns sabbat threat counters
...
Pass

6. MethA has option to respond
Adds stealth via bonding (or whatever)
Pass

7. MethB has option to respond
Enhanced Senses
Pass

8. MethC has option to respond (Eagle's Sight,Bauble, whatever...)
Pass

9. MethD has option to respond
Plays Sup. Eagle Sight on VampD
Pass

10.MethE has option to respond
Pass

11.MethA has option to respond
MethA plays Lost in crowds

12.MethB has option to respond
Pass

Block Fizzles?

13.MethC has option to respond
VampC attempts to block.
MethC plays enhanced senses.
(MethC fails to draw more intercept or to play it)
Pass

Block fizzles?

14.MethD has option to respond
VampD attempts to block.
MethD plays enhanced senses.
MethD plays Venetian Conference (let's pretend it applies)
Pass

15.MethE has option to respond
Pass

16.MethA has option to respond
MethA plays Dawn operation
Pass

17.MethB has option to respond
Pass

18.MethC has option to respond
MethC plays Venetian Conference
Pass

19.MethD has option to respond
Cancels block attempt
Pass

Block no longer exists

20.MethE has option to respond
Pass

Action resolves, to the chagrin of all parties.

So we see MethC had a vamp capable of blocking, but is afforded no
opportunity to do so because of action-response flow, correct?

Makes sense to me.

Now here's something that doesn't...

0. MethA declares start of minion phase
1. MethA declares end of minion phase

If other meths wanted to burn sabbat threat counters, when does that
option come in and in response to what? Are declaring the beginning
and ending of a phase akin to an undirected action or do they allow a
meth to completely bypass a phase (as far as other meths are
concerned, as they cannot play effects in between like bauble or
threat counters). Obviously reaction cards can only be played in
response to actions, so those are excluded from the discussion.

> meth to completely bypass a phase (as far as other meths are
> concerned, as they cannot play effects in between like bauble or
> threat counters). Obviously reaction cards can only be played in

Declarations of phases are not events.
They aren't under any single Methuselah's control.
When all pass in one stage, all move on to the next stage.

While recursive looping was something I originally considered, I did
not think you would actually say that's the correct mechanic because
of the problems (and more importantly, COMPLEXITY) recursion brings. I
now have a host of timing questions!

Q1: Is MethA always first to respond in all events during her
mainphase?

1. MethA enters minion phase
2. MethA passes
3. MethB Burns threat counters
(First opportunity to respond is MethA or MethC?)

Now that Q1 is answered, onto the paradoxes created -

Q2: Can you respond to a pass?

According to the model, it seems like you might be able to, but in
practice you cant, it would create infinite recursion with the person
who passed.

(If MethA always responds first as per Q1)
1. MethA enters minion phase
2. MethA passes
2.1 MethA has the opportunity and passes in response to 2.
2.1.1 MethA passes in response to 2.1
2.1.1.1 MethA passes in response to 2.1.1
2.1.1.1.1 MethA passes in response to 2.1.1.1
......... ad infinitum

It really doesnt matter who acts first, as the first response chain
would end up in a infinite logical procedural recursion.

Messages.Author: Timlagor
Messages.Body:
VTES2004 expounded:


Now you're just being silly. You simply play an infinite pass ;P

Anyway, clearly you never get to react to your own pass -nor in fact
does anyone ever 'react' to a pass; they merely get the opportunity to
act as a result of the pass. Meth A DOES NOT get an opportunity to react
to Meth B's pass: it moves on through C, D and E then (if all pass) to
the next phase.

>>1. Meth A passes.
>>2. Meth B gest opportunity to burn threat counters or whatever.
>>...
>>
>>Declarations of phases are not events.
>>They aren't under any single Methuselah's control.
>>When all pass in one stage, all move on to the next stage.
>>No Methuselah can bypass a stage.
>
>
> While recursive looping was something I originally considered, I did
> not think you would actually say that's the correct mechanic because
> of the problems (and more importantly, COMPLEXITY) recursion brings. I
> now have a host of timing questions!

There is no recursion.
There is iteration.

When an effect is played (the opposite of "pass"), abort the current
cycle and restart (iterate) - you do not suspend the cycle, recurse,
and then resume.

> Q1: Is MethA always first to respond in all events during her
> mainphase?

See 1.6.1.6

> 1. MethA enters minion phase
> 2. MethA passes
> 3. MethB Burns threat counters
> (First opportunity to respond is MethA or MethC?)

MethA. See 1.6.1.6

> Now that Q1 is answered, onto the paradoxes created -
>
> Q2: Can you respond to a pass?

No.
A pass is the opposite of an effect.
Effects are responded to (by restarting the 1.6.1.6 queue).


